## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Sekhiya 41 of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (entitled *Anāhaṭa*, translated as "Opening the mouth") is an etiquette training rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka regulating monastic decorum during meals, specifically proscribing the opening of the mouth before food has been brought to it. An English translation of the text and its case narrative is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali. No discussions of this rule appear in the provided secondary literature.

 It corresponds to rule 41 of the Theravāda *Bhikkhupātimokkha*, the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, and the *Parivāra*, as well as bhikkhu and bhikkhunī rules preserved in Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese across the Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, Mahāsāṅghika, Mahīśāsaka, Mūlasarvāstivāda, and Sarvāstivāda traditions, in addition to the *Upāliparipṛcchā*.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
